title: The trans-Atlantic slave trade is estimated, not enumerated person by person

body: The SlaveVoyages project publishes both voyage records and estimates of the whole trans-Atlantic trade. Its overview says that some 12.5 million enslaved people were shipped from Africa and 10.7 million arrived in the Americas. The estimates table consulted for 1501–1866 summed people embarked to 12,521,354. Those totals are not a list of named individuals. The project's methodology essay explains that documented voyages are incomplete, especially before 1700, and that the estimates fill gaps for voyages that left no surviving record. The same project notes that other estimates of the volume exist. A higher or lower assumption about missing voyages changes the total. The trade was carried under several European flags and by merchants in the Americas, and the people embarked came from many African regions, not from one port. The database is the evidence. A round number repeated without the edition and the method is not.
